note: The five committed copy mutants behind AC-10A-12-ROLE-PA. Each `read` is inserted after the anchor line of districtRole() and is followed by its `guard`, so the mutant reads the shipped `role` column and returns it BEFORE the derivation: it compiles, runs, and agrees with the derivation on all 105 districts. That is the point - the difference is only visible in the source. The same file feeds the test (test/placement/role-column-scan.ts) and the kill harness (scripts/mutants-t10a-12-role.mjs), so the committed mutants and the mutants that are proven KILLED cannot drift apart.

mutants.shape: a member read, with the row type naming the column
mutants.read: const roleCol = (flagsJson as { districts?: { distId: string; role: string }[] }).districts?.find((r) => r.distId === d.id)?.role;

mutants.shape: a member read with no `role:` key anywhere
mutants.read: const roleCol = ((flags ?? {}) as unknown as Record<string, unknown>).role as DistrictRole | undefined;

mutants.shape: a shorthand destructuring binding (the shape QA used against the old regex)
mutants.read: const { role } = (flagsJson as any).districts.find((r: { distId: string }) => r.distId === d.id);

mutants.shape: a bracket read with the string literal as the key
mutants.read: const roleCol = (flagsJson as any).districts.find((r: { distId: string }) => r.distId === d.id)?.['role'] as DistrictRole | undefined;

mutants.shape: a computed-key read: the column name is held in a variable
mutants.read: const roleKey = 'role'; const roleCol = (flagsJson as any).districts.find((r: { distId: string }) => r.distId === d.id)?.[roleKey] as DistrictRole | undefined;
